BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Scope:** This reviews the Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the Wattlebridge playbook. It is a working analysis for the deal team and should be checked by NSW-qualified counsel before it goes to the Seller. The Seller's "negotiated" positions are Seller proposals, not agreed terms. Nothing in the Seller package has been approved by Amelia Frost.

## 1. Headline issues

The Seller's package would leave Wattlebridge with little practical recourse. The most serious problems are:

- **Disclosure and buyer knowledge** (Schedule 7, DL 1.1/1.2, cl 8.3) would deem the whole data room, the accounts and public registers disclosed, and bar claims over anything the Buyer or its advisers "knew" or could discover. This would hollow out the warranties.
- **Fundamental/title claims** would be pulled into the general regime, so title and capacity would carry the 20% cap and 18-month limit.
- **Thresholds** would make small claims unrecoverable and turn the basket into a deductible.
- **Fraud is not carved out.** The limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **The known risks are unprotected.** Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and Ironquay are handled by post-signing or post-completion mechanisms, or by no mechanism at all.

## 2. Departures from playbook and pushback

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m. 20% is a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None given. | Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal the fallback in the mark-up. |
| **De minimis / basket (12.2)** | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; only the excess above the basket is recoverable | De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; first-dollar recovery once exceeded | Reject. The Seller's version is a deductible that would leave most realistic claims unrecovered. |
| **General claims period (12.3/13)** | 18 months; any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). The "applies to all" wording is a hidden general-regime override. | Reject 18 months and the override. Counter at 24 months. |
| **Fundamental / title (incl. capacity)** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. Title and capacity must sit in their own regime. |
| **Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5)** | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this. | Reject. Require an express fraud carve-out. Counsel should also check enforceability of non-reliance and exclusion wording under NSW law and the Australian Consumer Law. |
| **Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2)** | Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, statutory registers and public records disclosed generally | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2 in full. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties. DL 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable only if it does not limit our claims. |
| **Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)** | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | Delete cl 8.3. Pro-sandbagging wording may be proposed as a fallback only if counsel approves. Specific indemnities must survive regardless of knowledge. |
| **Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)** | Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. | Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. | Reject. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (about 30%) of FY26 revenue. The DL states there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. Make effective consent plus condition evidence a condition precedent. Note the tension with DL 1.4, which says no consent is "legally required," when DD-002 contains a change-control clause. Treat that as a factual point to be resolved. |
| **Riverlark (cl 2/7)** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion | Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. | Reject post-completion release. Require a payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, and PPSR and security releases at Completion. The DL confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included. |
| **Employee bonuses (DL 5; DD-005)** | "A matter for the Seller." AUD 420k not in funds flow. On-costs not stated. | AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them. | Reject. Require either an itemised Completion deduction or Seller funding, including on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation). Clarify who bears the cost if continued-employment conditions fail. |
| **Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way. | Reject as inadequate. Broaden to cover IP title and transfer defects, third-party claims and cure costs. Keep the SOW3 cure: payment plus a confirmatory assignment. Verify payment status independently. Do not assume the AUD 180k is correct or incorrect. |
| **Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6; Sch 6; DL 6; DD-006)** | "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | Do not characterise it as a breach or put a number on it. Require log preservation, a forensic or scoped investigation, regular updates, and a specific indemnity or covenant. Counsel should assess whether the Privacy Act notifiable data breach scheme could be engaged once the scope is known. |
| **Sandbar renewals (DL 8; DD-008/011; AUD 330k)** | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | Ask for evidence on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and read DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing. Do not reclassify as Debt or deduct from price by default. |
| **Tax / IP (Seller update)** | Settled under the general regime | Remain OPEN. Do not assume unlimited liability or resolution. | Reject the general regime as settling them. Mark both as open and reserve the position. |
| **Title (cl/DL 10; DD-012)** | Title evidenced by the Company share register | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required. DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. | Reject. Require an ASIC company extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches, a register of members inspection, and evidence of transfer and authority. DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified title. |
| **Office lease (DL 7; DD-007)** | Notification obligation only | Not expressly covered; keep categories separate | Ask whether landlord consent is needed for a change of control. Obtain the lease clause and, if required, consent as a condition. |
| **Mossvale (DL 9; DD-009)** | Assignment restriction; consent not stated as required | Not expressly covered; keep categories separate | Obtain Mossvale's position in writing and confirm whether a share sale triggers the restriction. |
| **Disclosure currency** | Data room as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026 | Not specified | Today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure and refreshed data room as at signing. |

## 3. Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's package in its current form.** Do not describe any of the Seller's "negotiated" positions as agreed, and do not signal the 20% cap or the 18-month period as acceptable.
2. **Reset the commercial terms to the playbook:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k first-dollar basket; 24-month general period.
3. **Create a separate fundamental/title regime** (100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar), covering title, capacity and authority.
4. **Add an express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, and remove the "applies to all Claims" override.
5. **Limit disclosure to specific, fair disclosure.** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2, and reject deemed disclosure of the data room and public records.
6. **Delete cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge).** Preserve specific indemnities and title, capacity and fraud claims regardless of knowledge.
7. **Make Bluefen a condition precedent:** effective written consent, evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, and no consent-on-delivery.
8. **Require a Riverlark payout at Completion,** with repayment from Completion funds and security releases. Reject any post-completion release absent an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Itemise the AUD 420k bonuses and on-costs** as a specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded item.
10. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** to cover IP title and transfer defects, keep the SOW3 cure, and independently verify payment status.
11. **For the privacy incident,** require log preservation, investigation and updates, plus a specific indemnity or covenant. Make no breach or quantum assertions.
12. **For Sandbar,** request evidence on terminability and timing. Make no automatic Debt or price adjustment.
13. **Treat tax and IP as open** and reserve the position.
14. **Obtain independent title evidence** (ASIC extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches, register inspection, authority documents) rather than relying on DD-012.
15. **Clarify the lease and Mossvale consent positions** in writing, and require a bring-down disclosure as at signing.

**Immediate next steps:** Route the Seller's draft to counsel for NSW-law review. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback has been authorised and that none will be signalled in the mark-up. Issue the Buyer's requests on title, Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses first, since these are closing-critical.
